name: Do basement partition walls in the Denver area need floating bottom plates?

mainEntity.name: Do basement partition walls in the Denver area need floating bottom plates?

acceptedAnswer.text: Building a partition wall in a basement across the Denver metro area requires careful management of concrete slab movement. Many Front Range soils contain expansive bentonite clay that causes basement floor slabs to heave upward independently of structural foundation footings. To prevent cracked drywall or warped ceilings, basement partition walls should be built with floating bottom plates—leaving an intentional gap (typically 1.5 to 3 inches) secured with specialized framing spikes or slip clips. This separation lets the concrete slab shift without pushing framing into the upper floor joists.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, basement partition walls in the Denver area frequently require floating bottom plates to prevent expansive soil heave from buckling walls into overhead joists.
